value.note: The board has no non-plated holes: it carries no mounting holes, because it hangs from J1 on the Raspberry Pi's P1 pins and the Pi's own holes are two on revision 2.0 and none on revision 1.0. KiCad still emits the file, and it still has to be in the archive and named correctly - it just has nothing in it. Requiring payload here would mean adding a hole the design does not want.

gates.title: Routing obeys the permitted angle style
gates.reason: 159 corners are not on the permitted [0.0, 45.0] degree geometry [advisory: Octolinear style, on a board whose architecture is polar. The supply ring follows a circle, sixteen data spokes and sixteen clock arms run on radii, and the clock trunks walk a ring: none of that lands on a 0/45 degree turn, and forcing it to would make the geometry worse, not the board better. The manufacturable concern in this measurement is the acute corner, and tools/check_routes.py reports those separately. Kept as a measurement so a genuine regression is still visible.]

measurements.advisory_blocking_reason: 159 corners are not on the permitted [0.0, 45.0] degree geometry

gates.title: No unjustified sub-minimum track fragments
gates.reason: 85 track fragments below 0.25 mm are not pad or via entries [advisory: Every ordinary net on this board is routed by KiCad Routing Tools, and its fine-grid tap retries emit 0.07 to 0.14 mm legs where an escape is tight. Those retries are what make the escapes route at all, the router offers no setting to coarsen them, and shortening the fragments afterwards would mean editing routed copper by hand - which this board's process forbids. No fragment is a sliver in copper: they are collinear continuations at full track width.]

measurements.advisory_blocking_reason: 85 track fragments below 0.25 mm are not pad or via entries

process.name: JLCPCB ordinary ink via plugging (tented/plugged vias)
process.rule: Minimum distance from a plugged via to an adjacent solder-mask opening (pad) so the ink dam is retained.
process.interpretation: Measured from the via annular-ring edge to the nearest solder-mask aperture edge, on the same board side. Vias whose annulus intersects an aperture cannot be plugged at all and are reported separately.
